pass_a_gloss: For this is the being seen as in a form of fire by night, yet in a form of cloud by day. For it was necessary, necessary for those still infants to have illumination and shining that carries off unto God-knowledge; yet for those above these and made bright through the faith, shelter and help, so that they might be able to carry through nobly the present life’s heat and the day’s burden: ‘For all who wish to live piously in Christos / Christ will be persecuted.’ And when the cloud sets out, the tent also sets out together, and when it settles it is set down together, and with it those from Israel were doing this; for the Church follows Christ everywhere, and the holy multitude of those believing is not separated from the one calling unto salvation. Palladius: And what would our setting-out and settling be understood as, perhaps, Christos / Christ leading forward and leading? Cyril: The word will somehow be indifferent for us in these things at least, the wishing to be with God of both setting out together and settling down together with the cloud showing us as it were some type; yet casting the mind into meanings as thin as possible, we will say that again: that first setting-out is the from unbelief unto faith, and from ignorance unto knowledge, and from not knowing who the one by nature and truly God is, unto knowing clearly the Master and Maker of all. And a second and beneficial setting-out as it were after that is the from baseness and licentiousness unto wishing already somehow to do and think the better things. And a third more advanced than this and in greater good-repute is the from the lacking unto the having-aright, both practically and dogmatically at once. Or do we not go by little toward the growth understood in Christos / Christ, advancing unto a perfect man, and springing up also unto the measure of the age of his fullness? This is perhaps somewhere what is hymned to us through divine Paul’s voice: ‘Forgetting the things behind, and stretching out to the things before, according to a mark I pursue unto the prize of the upward calling.’ And setting out intelligibly from ignorance unto recognition, from unlearning unto understanding, from unbelief unto faith, and always advancing in virtues, do we not change harbor from place to place, and transferring from such a disposition or habit perhaps unto such another already somehow resemble those accustomed to journey? Palladius: I understand what you say. Cyril: Yet neither the setting-out from baseness, nor indeed reaching and somehow lodging among the better things, would anyone be able to set right, unless Christos / Christ being together and leading. Therefore he also was saying to the holy disciples: ‘Without me you are not able to do anything.’ Therefore both being with God, and doing all things with him, would hint enigmatically then at setting out together when the cloud sets out, and resting together when it is still. Yet, through the Lord’s command
